_comment: ff_fuel (brief D1, issues #32 and #37, patches/ff_fuel/): the flex-fuel
state block plus the stock signals the E0 equivalence run compares.
patches/ff_fuel/test/procedure.md is the full bench procedure; this file
is only the variable list it needs.
Addresses of the ff_* variables come from patches/ff_fuel/patch.json
build.ram (0x7FFB00, 0x100 B) plus the offsets documented in
patches/ff_fuel/src/ff_state.h.  READ THEM OUT OF patch.json, not out of
this file, the day the block moves:
python3 logging/med9log.py log --session logging/sessions/ff_fuel.json \
--patch patches/ff_fuel/patch.json --bus gs_usb:0 --seconds 120 \
-o logs/2026-xx-xx_ff_fuel.csv
resolves every patch_offset against build.ram and overrides the addresses
below.
Checks, in order (procedure.md sections 2-5):
1. ff_magic == 0x46463031 ('FF01') and ff_length == 64.  If they are
zero the hook never ran: look at ff_src_seen first.
2. ff_src_seen answers scheduler.md 11.7 in one sample: 1 = only the
task-set-A hook (0x432940) fires, 2 = only the set-B hook (0x12067C),
3 = both (which the OS should make impossible).  ff_src_owner is the
one that actually ticks.
3. ff_ticks rises by about 100 per second (the raster is 10 ms, not
100 ms - C4, issue #44).  It must track raster_setA_10ms_count or
raster_setB_10ms_count 1:1, whichever set is live.
4. With no Pico on the bus: ff_mode == 3 (FAULT), ff_e_filt == 0 and
ff_f_q10 == 1024.  1024 is the bit-identical-to-stock value, so this
is also the E0 equivalence condition.
5. With the Pico running: ff_frames rises, ff_mode == 1 (OK),
ff_e_filt follows the frame at no more than 2 %/s, ff_f_q10 follows
ff_F_curve, and ff_rk_calls rises with engine speed (it counts
segments, not raster activations).
6. (D2, #39) The same four numbers are visible without a logger:
`21 6F` = VCDS measuring block 111 is ff_diag_e_pct, ff_diag_f_pct,
the fuel temperature and 256*ff_persist_state + ff_mode.  Rehearse it
with  python3 logging/med9log.py groups --sim
--sim-dump work/ff_fuel.bin 111
7. (D2, #38) eep_blk8_mirror_b0 IS the stored ethanol percent: it is the
block manager's RAM mirror of EEP_CONF block 8 payload +0.  It must
equal ff_e_persist whenever ff_persist_state is 2, 3 or 4, and the
block checksum eep_blk8_mirror_csum must satisfy
sum(bytes +0..+29) + csum == 0xFFFF at every sample.  Read them over
DDLI (21 F0); RequestUpload (0x35) refuses that window, DDLI does not
(kwp.md 4.3 and 5).
8a. (E1, #34) The ignition blend. `21 6C` = VCDS measuring block 108 is
f_zw in %, dzw_e in degCA, the worst of the six dwkrz bytes in degCA
and 0x7FD31B & 3. With the shipped calibration (ff_zw_enable = 0) the
first two MUST read 0 and zwist_display_b1 must match the stock
baseline sample for sample. With the blend on, ff_dzw_e must go to 0
on the first activation the mode leaves OK/HOLD - no hold, no ramp -
while ff_f_q10 is still held; that asymmetry is the whole of #37.
The calibration loop and the KFZWOP-KFZW budget table are
patches/ff_fuel/test/procedure_e1.md.
8. (D2, #38) ff_persist_writes rises by at most 1 per minute and
ff_persist_fails stays 0.  ff_persist_err is the block manager's own
code: 1 queued, 2 done, 0x80 device failure, 0x82 checksum failure
(eeprom.md 8.3).  ff_persist_wait counts the rate limit down at 100/s.
Record the same variables on the STOCK image first: that baseline and the
ff_fuel log are what tools/logcmp.py compares with
patches/ff_fuel/test/tolerance.json.
E2 (issue #35, 2026-09-17) added ff_fst_q10 and ff_zwst_add - the two
values the three start stubs consume - and the stock cells a cold-start
series needs: tmst, ksta_adapted, zwstt, B_st, B_stend, anztist, zdgz,
the after-start timer and the bank-1 lambda correction.  ff_length is
now 68 and the checksum covers TWO ranges; see ff_state.h.
patches/ff_fuel/test/procedure_e2.md is the recipe that uses them.
rlsol_req and rl_max_arb come from brief E3's naming pass (VCDS ids 375
and 2051) and are stock signals, not ours.

vars.name: ff_magic
vars.notes: 0x46463031 = 1179599921 once ff_state_init() has run

vars.name: ff_length
vars.notes: 68 since brief E2 (#35) appended the second core range; 64 under the D2/E1 blob. Together with the magic and the csum it is the cold-start marker, and a block written by an older blob fails this check and is re-initialised

vars.name: ff_csum
vars.notes: bit-complement of the 16-bit byte sum of the TWO checksummed ranges, +0x08..+0x2B then +0x40..+0x43 (E2). The annex +0x2C..+0x3F is outside it

vars.name: ff_e_filt
vars.notes: filtered ethanol, 1/16 % per LSB, 0..1600 counts

vars.name: ff_f_q10
vars.notes: the fuel mass factor the rk hook applies; 1024 = 1.000 = stock

vars.name: ff_mode
vars.notes: 0 INIT, 1 OK, 2 HOLD, 3 FAULT, 4 OFF, 5 OVERRIDE

vars.name: ff_status
vars.notes: byte 7 of the last frame: 0 OK, 1 fault, 2 contaminated, 3 not ready; 255 = no frame yet

vars.name: ff_e_raw
vars.notes: byte 0 of the last frame, unfiltered

vars.name: ff_t_fuel
vars.notes: byte 1 of the last frame, degC + 40

vars.name: ff_frame_ctr
vars.notes: byte 3 of the last frame; frozen for 3 frames -> FAULT

vars.name: ff_fw_ver
vars.notes: byte 6 of the last frame: the Pico firmware version

vars.name: ff_cal_mode
vars.notes: ff_mode as read from FFCAL001: 0 off, 1 normal, 2 bench override

vars.name: ff_cal_ok
vars.notes: 1 = FFCAL001 magic, version, length and checksum all accepted

vars.name: ff_age_ticks
vars.notes: activations since the last good frame; x ff_tick_ms = ms

vars.name: ff_hold_ticks
vars.notes: activations left of the 60 s FAULT hold; 6000 at entry

vars.name: ff_frames
vars.notes: good frames since power-up, saturating; +10/s with the Pico running

vars.name: ff_faults
vars.notes: FAULT entries since power-up; 1 before the first frame arrives is normal

vars.name: ff_stall
vars.notes: consecutive frames with an unchanged rolling counter

vars.name: ff_src_owner
vars.notes: 1 = the task-set-A hook (0x432940) ticks, 2 = the set-B hook (0x12067C)

vars.name: ff_src_seen
vars.notes: bit0 set A has fired, bit1 set B has fired. This one sample answers scheduler.md 11.7

vars.name: ff_src_foreign
vars.notes: consecutive calls from the non-owner hook; must stay 0 in normal running

vars.name: ff_ticks
vars.notes: periodic activations since power-up; +100/s, tracks the live 10 ms raster counter 1:1

vars.name: ff_e_key
vars.notes: the value the FAULT decay aims at; 0 (E0) until brief D2 loads it from EEPROM block 8

vars.name: ff_e_frac
vars.notes: sub-count of ff_e_filt, 1/1024 of a 1/16 % count; carries the 0.32-count slew step

vars.name: ff_frame_bad
vars.notes: 1 = the last frame was rejected (implausible E%, status 1/3, a stalled counter or a wrong id echo). It LATCHES until the next good frame, because at 10 Hz frames and a 100 Hz raster nine activations out of ten see nothing

vars.name: ff_dzw_e
vars.notes: THE ignition offset: what the stub at 0x41D40C adds to zwgru every ignition event, s8, 0.75 degCA per count, positive = advance. It is 0 whenever ff_zw_enable is 0, the calibration is not usable, ff_e_filt is 0, or ff_mode is not OK/HOLD/OVERRIDE - and on the FIRST activation the mode leaves OK/HOLD, with no hold and no ramp (the #37 ignition rule). Also measuring block 108 field 2. Log this rather than the measuring block when you need the 10 ms resolution of a fault step

vars.name: ff_fzw_q8
vars.notes: f_zw(ff_e_filt) from ff_fzw_curve, 1/256 per count, 0..255 (255 = 0.996, the u8 maximum). It is the factor ff_dzw_map was scaled by, so ff_dzw_e ~ ff_fzw_q8 * map / 256. Zero whenever the blend is not producing, so fields 1 and 2 of block 108 always agree. Also measuring block 108 field 1

vars.name: ff_rk_calls
vars.notes: segment-task invocations of the rk hook; rises with engine speed, 0 with the engine off

vars.name: ff_e_persist
vars.notes: the E% the patch believes is in EEP_CONF block 8: read back at cold start, then whatever the last commit staged. 65535 = nothing known (an erased or implausible store), which is what makes the first commit pass the hysteresis

vars.name: ff_persist_state
vars.notes: 0 idle, 1 staged, 2 committing, 3 done, 4 error. Also the A byte of measuring block 111 field 4

vars.name: ff_persist_err
vars.notes: the last nvm_block_request return or request status: 2 = done, 1 = queued, 0x40 queue full, 0x80 device failure, 0x82 checksum failure, 0x81/0x83 refused (eeprom.md 8.3)

vars.name: ff_diag_e_pct
vars.notes: ff_e_filt rounded to whole percent; measuring id 2196, block 111 field 1

vars.name: ff_diag_f_pct
vars.notes: (ff_f_q10 * 100) >> 10, so 100 = stock and 154 = F 1.54; measuring id 2197, block 111 field 2

vars.name: ff_diag_t_degc
vars.notes: a copy of ff_t_fuel (degC + 40); measuring id 2198, block 111 field 3, where it is emitted as formula 0x05 with B = value + 60

vars.name: ff_persist_wait
vars.notes: activations left of the ff_persist_rate_s window; 6000 right after a commit and after power-up, counting down at 100/s

vars.name: ff_persist_writes
vars.notes: commits that finished with status 2, saturating. At most one per ff_persist_rate_s

vars.name: ff_persist_fails
vars.notes: commits that did not; must stay 0. Anything else means the EEPROM or its driver is unhappy - stop and read ff_persist_err

vars.name: eep_blk8_mirror_b0
vars.notes: EEP_CONF block 8 payload +0 in the block manager's RAM mirror - the stored ethanol percent itself. This is the variable issue #38 is about: it must survive a battery disconnect. DDLI reads it; RequestUpload refuses the window

vars.name: eep_blk8_mirror_b14
vars.source: re/findings/eeprom.md section 4 (the one stock client, cpu 0x134380)
vars.notes: the only byte of block 8 stock code touches. Log it to prove the patch did not disturb it

vars.name: eep_blk8_mirror_b29
vars.source: re/findings/eeprom.md section 5 (flags & 3 != 0: the manager owns payload len-3)
vars.notes: the manager's own byte; the patch must never write it

vars.name: eep_blk8_mirror_csum
vars.notes: sum(payload +0..+29) + this == 0xFFFF at every sample; the stage keeps it correct incrementally

vars.name: nvm_queue_state
vars.notes: the block manager's request-queue state: 0x20/0x21 idle, 0x23-0x27 a request in progress. It should be idle in almost every sample

vars.name: raster_setA_10ms_count
vars.notes: set A 10 ms epilogue; +100/s if set A is live

vars.name: raster_setB_10ms_count
vars.notes: set B 10 ms epilogue; +100/s if set B is live

vars.name: raster_setB_1ms_count
vars.notes: +1000/s; the time reference for every slope in this session

vars.name: rk_fuel_mass
vars.notes: the cell the rk hook scales. Stock vs patched at E0 must be identical sample for sample

vars.name: dwi_inj_angle
vars.notes: the injection window signal: rk x 1.5 raises this by ~50 %

vars.name: zwist_display_b1
vars.notes: the final angle, bank 1, after the knock retard, zwmin and the -54..+58.5 degCA clamp. With ff_dzw_e = 0 it must match the stock baseline sample for sample; with the blend on it must move by exactly ff_dzw_e unless a downstream limit binds. VCDS group 003 field 4

vars.name: dwkrz_0
vars.notes: per-cylinder knock retard, s8, <= 0, stored in FIRING order 1-5-3-6-2-4 (that mapping is COMMUNITY; the array itself is VERIFIED-STATIC). THE acceptance signal of docs/05 3.4: all six must stay 0 across a blend. VCDS groups 020-024

vars.name: dwkrz_5
vars.notes: measuring block 108 field 3 reports max() over these six, which does not depend on the cylinder order

vars.name: wkrm
vars.notes: the MEAN knock retard. This is the cell the stock low-octane-fuel detector 0x0F436C debounces against KFSWKFZK, so it is the early warning for the latch below

vars.name: zw_low_octane_latch
vars.notes: bit0 = the stock 'bad fuel' latch is ON (KFDZK retard is being applied through 0x80208E, on top of our offset), bit1 = it has recovered. On E85 bit0 must NEVER set: if it does, the dzw_E calibration asked for more advance than the fuel could take. Measuring block 108 field 4 reports these two bits

vars.name: rl_w
vars.notes: relative load, the KFZW column-axis input and the x input of ff_dzw_map. NOT the same cell as rl_for_fuel (0x7FED38), which is selected from it at 0x418A3C - log both when a cell of the ignition map does not seem to be the one being exercised

vars.name: prist_w
vars.notes: must stay above 13 bar (rail.md section 14) or three limp-home limits arm at once

vars.name: can_rx_spare0_b0
vars.notes: byte 0 of the raw frame in can_rx_shadow slot 15: proves reception independently of our state machine

vars.name: can_rx_spare0_ctr
vars.notes: byte 3, the rolling counter, straight out of the driver shadow

vars.name: ff_fst_q10
vars.notes: THE start fuel factor: what the two stubs at 0x41A680 and 0x41A808 multiply ksta_adapted (0x80302C) by while the start is in progress. 1024 = 1.000 = stock. It is 1024 whenever ff_st_enable is 0, the calibration is not usable, ff_e_filt is 0, or ff_mode is INIT/OFF - and it FOLLOWS ff_e_filt through the FAULT hold and decay, exactly as ff_f_q10 does (the fuel half of the #37 rule). Also measuring block 69 field 1

vars.name: ff_zwst_add
vars.notes: THE start ignition advance: what the stub at 0x431384 adds to zwstt (0x802096), s8, 0.75 degCA per count, always >= 0. It drops to 0 on the FIRST activation the mode leaves OK/HOLD/OVERRIDE, with no hold and no ramp (the ignition half of the #37 rule), and it is 0 at and above ff_zwst_tmax (tmst count 117 = 39.75 degC). Log this rather than the measuring block when you need 10 ms resolution on a fault step. Also measuring block 69 field 2

vars.name: tmst
vars.notes: engine temperature LATCHED at start; the column axis of ff_fst_map and the gate of ff_zwst_add. One writer (0x5BBAC), so it does not move during a start - which is what makes a start series comparable. Measuring block 69 field 3

vars.name: ksta_adapted
vars.notes: ksta * kstaa, the cranking lever: 1024 = 1.000. THIS is the cell the two S1 stubs publish, so patched/stock = ff_fst_q10 while the start is in progress. Forced to exactly 0x400 once B_stend is set - and note that the low-pressure %ESSTT publishes that 0x400 THROUGH the hooked store, which is why the stub gates on B_stend (start.md section 9.3). Measuring block 69 field 4, as a raw count

vars.name: zwstt
vars.notes: the start ignition angle. While B_stend is clear this byte REPLACES the whole per-bank angle in zwbas_per_bank - zwgru, the bank offsets AND the knock retard are bypassed. Patched minus stock must equal ff_zwst_add unless the +127 clamp binds. Compare against zwist_display_b1 below

vars.name: B_st
vars.notes: start attempt active; 1 while cranking

vars.name: B_stend
vars.notes: start finished, four cycles after 0x7FE920. THE gate of both S1 stubs and, through its segment copy 0x7FECCA, of the whole zwstt override. Everything E2 does happens while this is 0

vars.name: anztist
vars.notes: injections since start = clamp(0x7FD298 - 0x7FD26B, 0, 255); the x axis of the stock KFWKSTT decay. The natural time base of a start series - plot ksta_adapted against THIS, not against seconds

vars.name: zdgz
vars.notes: ignitions since start; the y axis of the stock KFZWSTT. The time base for the zwstt series

vars.name: tnst_w
vars.notes: after-start timer: incremented by afterstart_timer (0x0D0E54) while the engine turns, saturating, reset only at power-up. The tick PERIOD is not established from the dump - measure its slope against raster_setB_1ms_count in the first log and record it

vars.name: fr_w_b1
vars.notes: the lambda controller's multiplicative correction, bank 1, Q15 (32768 = 1.000). It is clamped out of the loop during the start, so it is a POST-start signal: watch it come back and settle near 1.0 after a start with f_st enabled. If it settles rich-correcting, ff_fst_map is too rich for the tail of the start

vars.name: rlsol_req
vars.source: re/symbols.csv (E3, issue #41); VCDS measuring id 375, handler 0x03C348 emits formula 0x21 with A = 0x80 and B = v >> 8, i.e. 100/32768 % per LSB
vars.notes: the charge REQUEST the torque coordinator produces (max(0x8034B8, rlsol_mdfue)). Added on brief E3's suggestion: it is the stock signal that says what the driver asked for, which is what a start or a window limit has to be read against

vars.name: rl_max_arb
vars.source: re/symbols.csv (B9, issue #17); VCDS measuring id 2051, handler 0x04574C emits formula 0x21 with A = 0xFF and B = (v * 255) >> 16, i.e. 100/65536 % per LSB
vars.notes: the ARBITRATED charge limit: min(0x80234C, the injection-window limit, 0x802358, 0x802360, 0x80235E), computed at 0x0C7CF8 and feeding the final limit 0x80360E. Added on brief E3's suggestion: together with dwi_inj_angle it is how you see the injection window bite before it costs torque
